answer: Each identity anchors to a registered handloom weaving ivory silk thread. The loom shuttle sensor signs a fresh tension-and-echo curve every epoch, bound to the epoch nonce and cross-checked against the weaving guild registry. One loom, one vote: two identities reporting the same echo collapse to one vote and burn a $50 stake. A farm wanting 100 votes must buy, house and run 100 real looms, about $600 each plus $50 a year in upkeep, each needing a season of logged weaving before it counts. No fresh signed curve, no vote; marginal cost rises linearly with n.
